messages:
maria-g: Heads up — NoraTech is seeing p95/p99 regressions since ~10:30 UTC. Our SLO alerts fired, p95 ~3x, p99 ~5x. Traces point at model-serving requests that miss the prefix/KV cache and fall back to full decode. Escalating here. https://dash.reddemo/noratech
akshay: Any recent deploys around that time? or config change to caching?
jordan: We rolled key-tagging for route sharding ~3h ago (small refactor). It touched how prefix keys are composed.
tilly-support: Customer on Dedicated (eu-west). They claim no traffic spike on their side. Ticket #CS-4729 opened.
li: Pasting counters from the node that handles their traffic — miss rate jumped after the key-tagging rollout:
```
kv_prefix_miss_total{zone="eu-west",node="node-17"} 124800
kv_prefix_miss_total{zone="eu-west",node="node-17",after_rollout="true"} 642300
kv_prefix_hit_ratio 0.12 -> 0.03
```
Also saw a lot of unique cache keys with tiny differences (ordering/duplicate tags).
maria-g: Example noisy keys (sanitized):
```
prefix:v1|route:chat|user:acct-1023|tags:lang=en,session=abc123
prefix:v1|route:chat|user:acct-1023|tags:session=abc123,lang=en
```
li: ^ that's the bug. Tag ordering isn't normalized before we build the cache key, so every permuted tag order becomes a different cache entry -> hotset explosion and eviction loop.
akshay: Oof. That would explain the thrash. Eviction churn + cache misses -> backend decode pressure -> p95 spike.
jordan: Repro steps I used locally:
1) send 50 concurrent requests for same logical input but randomize tag header order
2) observe distinct keys in /metrics under kv_prefix_keys_total
cURL snippet that reproduces the permutation:
```
curl -X POST https://api.reddemo/predict \
  -H "x-rd-tags: lang=en,session=abc123" \
  -d '{"input":"hi"}'
# then
curl -X POST https://api.reddemo/predict \
  -H "x-rd-tags: session=abc123,lang=en" \
  -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
tilly-support: Customer impact: increased latency by ~400-800ms for affected requests. They've escalated to AR.
li: Short-term mitigations we can toggle immediately:
- enable key normalization feature-flag (canonicalize tag order + dedupe) (fast rollback)
- bump prefix-cache-size for eu-west pool by 20% (reduces eviction pressure)
- temporary routing to a cold fallback variant that has more cache warmup
akshay: Can we flip normalization flag in <10m? If so do it and monitor p95. Also we should avoid increasing cache size blindly if memory is constrained.
maria-g: Ops-bot shows deployment window active.
ops-bot: deploy-check: canary-traffic=2%; recent-deploy=jordan/kv-tagging-refactor@2026-03-17T08:15Z; blocking_issues=0
jordan: I'll cut a quick patch that normalizes tags before key-building and add unit tests. Will also instrument a metric kv_key_normalized_total.
li: I pushed a canary with normalization off to node-18; flipping flag now in canary pool. Will report in 2 minutes.
li: Canary flip done. Early signs: key cardinality for the canary nodes down ~85% and p95 on canary traffic back near baseline.
akshay: Good. Plan: roll normalization to all node pools in eu-west, watch p95/p99 for 30m, then backfill hot keys into cache via warmup job.
maria-g: Coordination: tilly, tell NoraTech we have an active mitigation and timeline ~30-60m. akshay/jordan/li — please do the rollout and post status here.
tilly-support: Noted, messaging sent. They appreciated the quick update. :pray:
li: Follow-ups: create a small warmup job that iterates top 500 active keys and writes to prefix cache (ids from request logs). I'll draft a job and run in safe mode.
jordan: I'll ship the normalization patch + e2e test, then monitor for regressions. If anything goes wrong we can flip flag off and rollback the refactor commit.
akshay: Also let's add an alert for sudden spike in unique prefix key cardinality per node (new metric kv_prefix_key_cardinality) so we detect this earlier.
maria-g: Thanks everyone. Updating incident doc and CS ticket. Will close once p99 stabilizes for 60m.
ops-bot: alert-resolved candidate check: p95 eu-west decreased from 3x -> 1.1x in 18m. p99 trending down. Keep monitoring.
